## Overview

This is a chart built around an empty Life Palace in the Chou 丑 branch, which means the main stars that shape your character are borrowed from the opposite Travel Palace: Tian Tong (the easygoing star of comfort, enjoyment and contentment) and Ju Men (the eloquent communicator, quick with words and argument). Both are dim here, so these qualities tend to surface softly rather than loudly — you may feel the pull toward an easy life and toward explaining, debating and talking things through, without either being overwhelming in force. The Life Palace also holds Zuo Fu and You Bi, the two great auspicious helpers, plus Huo Xing and Di Kong, which add speed and restlessness and an instinct for the unconventional. The overall picture is a sociable, articulate, help-magnet personality that does better when it has companions and conversation, and less well when it has to grind alone.

For a newcomer: the Life Palace is the heart of the chart, the palace that describes you and how you move through the world. The Body Palace names the palace where your life energy shows up most concretely in later years — here it is the Wealth Palace, which contains Tai Yang (the sun, outward drive and visibility) and Tian Liang (the steady elder, resource, and protection), with Tian Liang carrying the birth-year Hua Ke, or recognition. So the Body Palace says your real field of action is work, resource and money: your identity gets built through what you provide and manage. The Five Element Bureau is Water 2, a quiet, adaptive, water-based frame that suits a life run by flow and negotiation more than force.

The two most distinctive traits: a strong reliance on other people (all six auspicious stars are concentrated in the Life, Siblings, Health and Parents palaces, not in the career or wealth palaces directly), and a mind that needs to talk, explain and travel — with an empty Life Palace, you take your colour from whoever and whatever surrounds you.

## Life Palace and Personality

The Life Palace in Ding Chou 丁丑 has no main stars of its own and borrows Tian Tong and Ju Men from the Travel Palace, both dim. Tian Tong is the comfort-seeker: it prefers harmony, good food, good company and a gentle pace. Ju Men is the talker and the reasoner, the star of speech, debate and explanation. With both dim, your default is not loud charisma but a pleasant, articulate, negotiating style — you tend to smooth things over with words, and you may get quietly tired of conflict rather than confront it head-on. Because these stars are borrowed rather than owned, you probably feel your character gets defined by circumstances and by the people around you more than by a fixed inner script.

Zuo Fu and You Bi in the Life Palace are the strongest asset in the chart: helpers who turn up, favours that come back, and a capacity to get support from both sides of a situation. Use them — this is a personality that thrives in collaboration and suffers in isolation. Huo Xing adds urgency and a short fuse when pressure builds; Di Kong adds a taste for the unusual and a suspicion of the conventional, plus a tendency to have resources that look plentiful but are hard to pin down. The practical counsel is to work with people rather than against them, to keep talking when things tighten, and to notice when Huo Xing is making you hurry a decision that would be better slept on.

## Career

The Career Palace in Ji Si 己巳 holds Tai Yin (the moon: sensitivity, planning, working away from the glare) in its fallen brightness, with Tuo Luo, one of the challenging stars, alongside. Fallen Tai Yin suggests that conventional, high-profile career paths may feel less natural than quieter, behind-the-scenes, planning, research, design or people-support roles — work where you prepare and refine rather than perform. Tuo Luo as pressure means career progress can feel like dragging a wheel uphill: slow, with setbacks that ask you to keep adjusting rather than break through with one dramatic push. Read it as a pace-setting star, not a bad omen — build in buffer time and don't judge yourself by a colleague's speed.

The Career Palace's opposite palace is the Spouse Palace with Tian Ji, so your working life and your partnership question each other; decisions about one often touch the other. Meanwhile the Body Palace sits in the Wealth-Palace, meaning your actual energy goes into resource and money-building rather than into title. In practice: choose work where steady competence is valued over visibility, and let your support stars do the networking for you.

## Wealth

The Wealth Palace in Gui You 癸酉 contains Tai Yang (the sun: outward drive, visibility, generosity) at neutral brightness and Tian Liang (the steady elder: resource, prudence, protection) at steady brightness, with the birth-year Hua Ke, or recognition, on Tian Liang — and this is also where the Body Palace sits. That combination is a good sign for earning through reputation and reliability rather than through sudden bursts: Tian Liang with Hua Ke means your prudence and resourcefulness get noticed, and steady, well-reviewed work tends to pay off in a stable way. Tai Yang suggests income connected to public-facing effort and to giving generously of your time; it also suggests you spend generously, so it is worth watching how much of the sun's warmth goes outward.

Di Jie in the Wealth Palace is the challenging note: it brings disruption to plans and a tendency for money matters to arrive in irregular chunks rather than smoothly. It is best handled by keeping clear records and reviewing your accounts regularly instead of trusting memory. The Spirit Palace, which is empty and borrows Tai Yang and Tian Liang from here, tells you inner contentment for you is largely built on the same prudence — you feel calm when savings and resources are in order. Lean into the Tian Liang side: careful, well-documented handling of money suits this chart far more than chasing quick outcomes.

## Love and Partnership

The Spouse Palace in Yi Hai 乙亥 holds Tian Ji (the strategist: clever, mobile, calculating, sometimes over-thinking) at neutral brightness, with no supporting stars listed. Tian Ji in the Spouse Palace tends to point to a partner who is intelligent and resourceful, and to a relationship that runs on mutual problem-solving and adjustment rather than on grand romance. It also suggests a certain amount of mental churn — two clever people can talk a small issue into a large one. The Spouse Palace's opposite palace is the Career Palace with Tai Yin (fallen), so time and attention given to work can quietly compete with time given to the relationship; naming that openly is more useful than letting it build.

Tian Ji, being mobile, favours partnerships that tolerate change — moves, shifts in schedule, changes of plan. The most workable approach is to keep conversation concrete and to decide together rather than separately. Note that the Friends Palace carries Tan Lang (the social charmer and networker) with birth-year Hua Quan, power — your social circle is lively and influential, which can be a support to partnership as long as friendship time doesn't crowd out the relationship itself.

## Wellbeing Habits

The Health Palace in Ren Shen 壬申 holds Wu Qu (the steady, disciplined worker) at steady brightness with the birth-year Hua Lu, prosperity, and Tian Xiang (the elegant minister, balanced and dignified) at brilliant brightness, with Tian Yue, an auspicious star, and Ling Xing, a challenging one. This is a strong Health Palace. Wu Qu with Hua Lu suggests that routine and discipline genuinely reward you — regular habits tend to feel good and pay off. Tian Xiang points to balance and moderation, and Tian Yue to having supportive people around you. Ling Xing is the challenging note: it adds intensity and a tendency to push hard when you are caught up in something, so build in regular pauses rather than marathon days.

For sleep: Wu Qu's discipline favours a fixed bedtime and wake time; Ling Xing's intensity is the reason to protect the hour before sleep from stimulating activity. For food: Tian Tong in the Life Palace enjoys comfort food and plenty of it, so the chart's own balance is Tian Xiang's moderation — regular, simple meals at regular times tend to suit you better than feasts. For movement: Wu Qu likes consistency, so a steady weekly routine beats occasional intense sessions, and Ling Xing suggests keeping the intensity moderate. For emotional balance: your empty Life Palace takes colour from your company, so choose calm, steady people to spend time with, and use Zuo Fu and You Bi in the Life Palace — talk to a trusted friend rather than carrying pressure alone. If you feel unwell, please consult a qualified healthcare professional.

## Family and Social Circle

The Friends Palace in Geng Wu 庚午 carries Tan Lang (the social charmer, appetite for life and people) at bright brightness with the birth-year Hua Quan, power. This is the loudest, most influential palace in your chart, and it is also your current Major Period. Your circle of friends is likely to be vivid, well-connected and a real source of influence in your life — other people's vitality genuinely moves your affairs. The caution with Hua Quan on a social star is that the circle can also carry rivalry and status games; keep friendships warm but keep your own decisions your own. Its opposite palace, the Siblings Palace, holds Zi Wei with Wen Chang and Tian Kui, so siblings or close peers have a dignified, cultured quality that can help you.

The Parents Palace in Bing Yin 丙寅 holds Po Jun (the pioneer who clears the old to build the new) at steady brightness, with Wen Qu carrying the birth-year Hua Ji, obstacle. Po Jun in the Parents Palace suggests an older generation that is reformist, independent and perhaps unsettled in its ways; Wen Qu with Hua Ji points to friction over words and documentation — misunderstandings in messages, paperwork, or the way things are expressed. The practical approach is to confirm important family matters in writing and to be patient with phrasing, rather than assuming ill intent. The Children Palace in Jia Xu 甲戌 holds Qi Sha (the bold fighter) at brilliant brightness, suggesting lively, determined younger people around you, and the Property Palace in Wu Chen 戊辰 holds Lian Zhen (the principled, sometimes strict star) and Tian Fu (the treasure-keeper) at brilliant brightness — your home and family base is a resource worth keeping organised.

## Major Period and Year by Year

You are in the Major Period of the Friends Palace in Geng Wu 庚午, ages 52–61 (about 2020–2029), with Tan Lang bright and carrying the birth-year Hua Quan, power. These ten years are focused on people: networks, alliances, the influence of your circle, and your own social power. The pace is lively rather than steady — Tan Lang is the appetite-driven star, so there is momentum, sociability, and a lot of activity, with the main task being to direct that energy rather than be carried by it. Because the Life Palace is empty and takes its tone from circumstance, this people-centred period may feel unusually defining.

The next Major Period moves to the Travel Palace in Xin Wei 辛未, ages 62–71 (about 2030–2039), with Tian Tong and Ju Men dim — a quieter, more mobile decade oriented toward movement, communication and comfortable exploration rather than social prominence.

Each annual pillar follows the Chinese lunar year and roughly matches the calendar year, so a year's tone begins around the turn of the lunar new year.

### 2026 丙午 · Bing Wu

The annual Life Palace is the Friends Palace with Tan Lang bright — the same palace as your Major Period, so this year doubles down on social themes: alliances, visibility among peers, and who you spend your energy with. This year's transformations give Hua Lu to Tian Tong in the natal Travel Palace, so travel, movement and easy exchanges are worth leaning into; Hua Quan goes to Tian Ji in the natal Spouse Palace, giving partnership and negotiation extra force, a good time to settle joint plans; Hua Ke goes to Wen Chang in the natal Siblings Palace, so written and considered communication with peers and siblings is favoured. Hua Ji falls on Lian Zhen in the natal Property Palace, which calls for care and a slower pace around home, property matters and the rules governing them — read things twice before agreeing.

### 2027 丁未 · Ding Wei

The annual Life Palace is the Travel Palace with Tian Tong and Ju Men, both dim — a year whose tone is movement, conversation and a certain pleasant indecision. Hua Lu goes to Tai Yin in the natal Career Palace, so quiet, preparatory career work tends to be well rewarded; Hua Quan goes to Tian Tong in the natal Travel Palace, giving travel and change of scene real momentum; Hua Ke goes to Tian Ji in the natal Spouse Palace, favouring thoughtful negotiation in partnership. Hua Ji falls on Ju Men in the natal Travel Palace, which calls for care with speech and travel arrangements — a year to say less and confirm more, especially in the second half when schedules get busy.

### 2028 戊申 · Wu Shen

The annual Life Palace is the Health Palace with Wu Qu and Tian Xiang — a year that draws attention to routine, balance and steady discipline, and which suits you well. Hua Lu goes to Tan Lang in the natal Friends Palace, so social and network matters bring warmth and opportunity; Hua Quan goes to Tai Yin in the natal Career Palace, giving quiet career effort real push; Hua Ke goes to You Bi in the natal Life Palace, so help from others is recognised and comes back to you. Hua Ji falls on Tian Ji in the natal Spouse Palace, which calls for care and patience in close partnership — build in deliberate unhurried conversation, particularly toward the end of the year.

### 2029 己酉 · Ji You

The annual Life Palace is the Wealth Palace with Tai Yang and Tian Liang, the palace of your Body Palace — a year about resource, provision and reputation, and a fitting one to review your plans carefully. Hua Lu goes to Wu Qu in the natal Health Palace, so steady habits pay off; Hua Quan goes to Tan Lang in the natal Friends Palace, giving your circle real influence in your affairs; Hua Ke goes to Tian Liang in the natal Wealth Palace, which favours careful, well-reviewed work being noticed. Hua Ji falls on Wen Qu in the natal Parents Palace, so documentation and wording with family or older figures deserves extra care — confirm things in writing.

### 2030 庚戌 · Geng Xu

A new Major Period begins this year: the Travel Palace, ages 62–71. The annual Life Palace is also the Children Palace with Qi Sha brilliant — a bold, determined, forward-moving tone, suited to setting direction for the decade ahead. Hua Lu goes to Tai Yang in the natal Wealth Palace, favouring visible, outward-facing effort; Hua Quan goes to Wu Qu in the natal Health Palace, giving routine and discipline real force; Hua Ke goes to Tai Yin in the natal Career Palace, so quiet career work is recognised. Hua Ji falls on Tian Tong in the natal Travel Palace, which calls for a slower pace in travel and movement — plan journeys generously and don't overpack the schedule.

## Guidance

- Lean on Zuo Fu and You Bi in your Life Palace: when a decision is hard, talk it through with a trusted person rather than solving it alone.
- Because your Body Palace sits in the Wealth Palace with Tian Liang under Hua Ke, keep clear, regular records of your resources and let reliability be your visible strength.
- In the Friends Palace period of ages 52–61, with Tan Lang bright and Hua Quan, choose your circle deliberately — the people around you carry real influence, so give your time to the ones who steady you.
- Work with Tuo Luo and Ling Xing as pace-setters, not obstacles: build buffer time into career plans and keep exercise and work sessions moderate rather than marathon-long.
- With Wen Qu under Hua Ji in the Parents Palace, confirm important family matters and paperwork in writing, and be patient with phrasing rather than assuming conflict.
